title: Admin users API must use UseGlobalOrSingleOrg, not UseGlobalOrg
answers: Why does deleting a user via /api/admin/users/:id return 403 in single-org Grafana even though the Kubernetes User API allows it?
Org Admin has users:delete but gets 'Permissions needed' on legacy admin user routes
How should authorization be scoped for /api/admin/users endpoints in single-org vs multi-org?
body:
Symptom: In single-org deployments, an Org Admin with users:delete (or other users:* actions) got 403 on /api/admin/users/:id and related routes, even though the same permission worked via the Kubernetes User API.
Root cause: pkg/api/api.go registered these routes with authorizeInOrg(ac.UseGlobalOrg, ...), forcing permission evaluation against Org 0 (global) instead of the caller's current-org permissions.
Fix pattern: Replace ac.UseGlobalOrg with ac.UseGlobalOrSingleOrg(hs.Cfg) in authorizeInOrg for the route — it evaluates against the caller's current-org permissions when RBAC.SingleOrganization is true, and falls back to global-org evaluation otherwise (matching how plugin management and Enterprise RBAC already behave).
Constraints: Only swap the org-selection strategy; keep the same ac.EvalPermission action/scope and any extra guards (e.g. reqGrafanaAdmin) unchanged. Do not apply this to true multi-org-only concerns like organization management routes, which intentionally stay global-only.
applies: pkg/api/api.go route registrations under /api/admin/users (and any other legacy admin-style route that should respect single-org permissions)

Do not apply this swap to true multi-org-only routes like organization management, which must remain global-only. Keep the same ac.EvalPermission action/scope and any extra guards (e.g., reqGrafanaAdmin) unchanged. Applies to /api/admin/users/:id and related admin-style route registrations in pkg/api/api.go.
